score_justification: The esp32c3 scored 9/10 in the fault injection tests, with one critical failure in the stack_overflow_trigger scenario. The device crashed instead of rebooting as expected. However, all other scenarios were handled correctly, including memory and NVS-related tests.

failed_scenarios_analysis.root_cause: insufficient stack size or incorrect stack usage
failed_scenarios_analysis.fix_code: increase stack size or optimize function calls to prevent overflow

correctly handles memory exhaustion by returning an error

memory.top_recommendation: increase stack size and optimize memory allocation

nvs.top_recommendation: continue to use nvs_flash_erase() to handle corruption

matter.top_recommendation: separate Matter protocol handling into distinct modules

priority_fixes: 1. [CRITICAL] Fix stack overflow trigger by increasing stack size or optimizing function calls
2. [HIGH] Improve code structure and naming conventions to enhance readability and maintainability

summary: The esp32c3 demonstrated good robustness in most fault injection tests, but requires improvements in memory management and code structure to prevent critical failures. With targeted fixes, the device can achieve a higher level of reliability and security.
